0.0.n: A humble way to refer to the speaker's own company in formal situations.

0.1.n: Marks the company as the target of the application.

0.2.n: Links 弊社へ to 志望動機, making the motivation specifically about applying to this company.

0.3.n: Combines with 動機 to describe why someone wants a position.

0.4.n: In 志望動機, this refers to the reason for seeking the job.

0.5.n: Marks 志望動機 as what the interviewer asks the applicant to explain.

0.6.n: The て-form of 教える plus ください makes a polite request for information.

1.0.n: Politely acknowledges the interviewer's request before answering.

1.2.n: Combines with まで to set the endpoint of the applicant's experience.

1.3.n: Sets 今 as the endpoint; 今まで means up to now.

1.4.n: Links 今まで to 実務経験, describing experience accumulated so far.

1.5.n: Combines with 経験 to refer to hands-on professional experience.

1.6.n: Together with 実務, this refers to knowledge gained through actual work.

1.7.n: Marks 実務経験 as what the applicant will put to use.

1.8.n: The connecting form of 活かす links this action to the next clause in a formal style.

2.0.n: Emphasizes improving beyond the applicant's current skill level.

2.1.n: Points back to skills associated with the practical experience just mentioned.

2.2.n: An English loanword; Japanese does not require a separate plural form here.

2.3.n: Marks スキル as what the applicant wants to improve.

2.4.n: The connecting form of 高める joins skill improvement to the following goal.

2.6.n: Before an adjective, より indicates a higher degree without naming a comparison target.

2.7.n: Describes the technical sophistication of the systems the applicant wants to develop.

2.8.n: Connects 高度 to システム so it can describe the noun.

2.9.n: An English loanword that can refer to one system or multiple systems.

2.10.n: Marks システム as what the applicant wants to develop.

2.11.n: 開発する becomes 開発したい by replacing する with したい to express desire.

2.12.n: Marks the preceding desire as the content of 思っております.

2.13.n: A humble, formal version of 思っています that presents the applicant's current intention politely.

3.0.n: A respectful term for the listener's company, commonly used in spoken interviews.

3.1.n: Connects 御社 to よう as part of the comparison 御社のように.

3.2.n: Used in のように to express a comparison rather than referring to a physical appearance.

3.3.n: Completes のように, letting the comparison describe how a company provides products.

3.4.n: A technical loanword for technology that processes and interprets images.

3.5.n: Lists examples without implying that computer vision and AI are the only technologies used.

3.6.n: The abbreviation for artificial intelligence combines with 技術 to describe a technology category.

3.7.n: Combines with AI to refer to artificial intelligence methods and tools.

3.8.n: Marks the listed technologies as what is utilized.

3.9.n: The past form of 活用する modifies 商品, describing products built using these technologies.

3.10.n: The preceding clause describes the technologies incorporated into these items.

3.11.n: Marks 商品 as what the company provides.

3.12.n: The plain form directly modifies 企業, identifying the kind of company.

3.13.n: A formal business word, described here by the entire preceding clause.

3.14.n: Marks the company as the setting for learning and taking on challenges in the next line.

4.0.n: A somewhat formal adjective that takes な before a noun.

4.1.n: Connects 新た to 技術 so it can describe the noun.

4.2.n: Refers to technical methods or knowledge the applicant wants to learn.

4.3.n: Marks 技術 as what the applicant wants to learn.

4.4.n: The connecting form of 学ぶ links learning to the following desire for challenges.

4.6.n: An adjective ending in い that directly describes 挑戦 without needing な.

4.7.n: Used with をする to express undertaking something demanding.

4.8.n: Marks 挑戦 as the activity the applicant wants to undertake.

4.9.n: The desire form of する combines with 挑戦を to express wanting challenges.

4.10.n: Introduces the applicant's goals as the reason for applying, with a softer tone than から.

4.12.n: Respectfully refers to the interviewer's organization, contrasting with 弊社 used by the interviewer.

4.13.n: Marks 御社 as the destination of the application.

4.14.n: Combines with いたしました to describe the act of applying for the job.

4.15.n: The polite past form of humble いたす replaces しました to show respect when describing one's own action.

0.lit: Please tell us the motivation for applying to our company.
0.tip: 弊社 humbly refers to the speaker's own company; the applicant uses 御社 for that same company.

1.lit: Yes. Putting to use practical work experience up to now,
1.tip: 活かし connects to what follows, so the sentence has not finished yet.

2.lit: Further enhancing those skills, I am thinking that I want to develop more advanced systems.
2.tip: たいと思っております presents a wish or intention in a humble, formal style suitable for interviews.

3.lit: At a company that, like yours, provides products utilizing computer vision and AI technology,
3.tip: Japanese places descriptions before nouns: 提供する企業 means a company that provides.

4.lit: Because I want to learn new technologies and take on new challenges, I applied to your company.
4.tip: 応募いたしました is a humble, polite way to describe your own completed application.
